## Results

- An identical agent resubmitted scores 93-150 rating points apart (noise floor ~125). A single leaderboard submission cannot resolve differences below ~150.
- Opponent-decklist posterior graded on 300 replays with both real decklists known: 99.7% prior coverage, top-1 accuracy 0.63 (turn 1), 0.84 (turn 3), 0.94 (turn 10), well calibrated. 80% of misidentifications are near-identical sister lists.
- Found three test-harness faults that invalidated recorded evidence: legal empty moves scored as forfeits for opponents only (24.9% vs 0%), an engine that was never actually seeded, and 300-game cells that flipped sign at 600 games. Example correction: Archaludon matchup 0.887 -> 0.32.
- Local self-play harness reports 0.892 against the encounter-weighted field where the ladder shows 0.519. The bias grows with how much piloting skill the opponent's deck needs (+0.25 to +0.78).
- Grader-environment probes found silent production failures: exec()-loaded main.py has no __file__, the last callable becomes the entry point, and a lazy import disabled search on every submission (0 -> 273 search calls after fix).
- An apparent 0.532 -> 0.294 drop against the plurality archetype (z=1.68) was killed as a rating-band confound without spending a submission. The win rate is monotone in opponent rating (0.750/0.533/0.368/0.000).
- Metagame mined from 146,376 decks over 16 days: ~120-204 distinct decklists, with the top 40 lists covering 94.4% of play.

## The problem

Build a program that plays a hidden-information card game against thousands of other agents. Five shared submissions a day and a ladder whose single reading carries about ±125 rating points of noise make every improvement hard to verify.

## What I built

Rule-based policy with 1-ply forward search. A hypergeometric Bayesian posterior over opponent decklists, built from 146k mined decks. Sequential probability ratio tests for agent changes. Instrument validation (symmetry, determinism, distribution checks against real replays). A ladder-episode store for rating-band-conditioned matchup and loss analysis.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

The same failure modes appear in combat-model and wargame analysis: a simulator whose scoring rule penalises only one side, 'paired' random seeds that are not paired, self-play benchmarks where shared errors cancel, and decisions read off a single stochastic run. The project quantifies each one and shows how it was caught.
:::

## Tools

Python, kaggle-environments, Bayesian inference (multivariate hypergeometric likelihood), SPRT (Wald), Perfect-Information Monte Carlo search, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, C++ engine build / LD_PRELOAD seeding
